facts.raw_span: Serological tests for amoebiasis and hydatid disease were negative
a 11 × 7.5 × 11.2 cm predominantly anechoic, thick-walled lesion arising from the inferior surface of the liver
low-level internal echoes and a homogeneous echogenic area in its superolateral portion
the gallbladder was not visualized separately
Serological tests for amoebiasis and hydatid disease were negative

low-level internal echoes and a homogeneous echogenic area in its superolateral portion
the gallbladder was not visualized separately

concepts.why: The patient has a predominantly anechoic, thick-walled lesion arising from the inferior surface of the liver, which is consistent with a liver cyst.
The patient has a liver cyst with turbid fluid, which suggests an infection.
The patient has symptoms such as low-grade fever, tenderness in the right hypochondrium, and turbid fluid, which are consistent with a pyogenic liver abscess.
Although serological tests for hydatid disease were negative, the patient has a cystic lesion in the liver, which could be a hydatid cyst.
It explains the presence of a liver cyst with negative serological tests for parasitic infections, indicating a non-parasitic origin of the cyst.

rationales.F03: Low-grade fever is more commonly associated with infected liver cysts and pyogenic liver abscesses.
rationales.F05: Hepatomegaly is a non-specific finding that can be associated with various liver conditions.
rationales.F08: Negative serological tests for amoebiasis and hydatid disease make hydatid cyst of the liver less likely.
rationales.F09: The presence of a large, thick-walled lesion arising from the liver is highly suggestive of a liver cyst or infected liver cyst.
rationales.F10: Low-level internal echoes and a homogeneous echogenic area are consistent with an infected liver cyst or pyogenic liver abscess.
rationales.F12: Turbid fluid is more commonly associated with infected liver cysts and pyogenic liver abscesses.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large, thick-walled, anechoic liver lesion and turbid fluid on aspiration, along with low-grade fever and tenderness, supports the diagnosis of an infected liver cyst, which is a more specific diagnosis than pyogenic liver abscess given the imaging characteristics.
